source: per-tensor bytes summed from workspace/campaign/records/runs/qwen38-27b/uniform-q4-v1/manifest.json (755 tensors). This is MEASURED from the artifact, not derived.
embed_excluded_why: Dense model reads every weight per token EXCEPT the embedding table, from which exactly one row is gathered.

lane_floor_was_wrong.why: The lane's floor excluded lm_head. Greedy argmax over a 248,320 vocabulary must read the full lm_head each token, and at 675 MB it cannot be cached. Its 1.817 GB shortfall is lm_head plus the embed table.

CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_CLAIM.i_claimed: Qwen3.8 is AT the bandwidth wall with essentially no kernel headroom.
CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_CLAIM.the_error: I compared it against the 320-411 GB/s control, but that control was measured in Q80's 10-of-512 GATHER shape. A gather is near the worst case for bandwidth; Qwen3.8 reads dense and sequential, the best case. The gather control does NOT bound a dense-sequential model, so it cannot establish that Qwen3.8 is at its wall.
CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_CLAIM.what_is_actually_true: Qwen3.8 achieves 49.6% of the 819 GB/s peak. Whether that is its ceiling is UNMEASURED.
CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_CLAIM.exact_missing_measurement: A no-model DENSE SEQUENTIAL bandwidth control on this box. If it lands near peak, Qwen3.8 has ~2x kernel headroom on top of the density lever; if it lands near 406 GB/s, my original claim was right for the wrong reason.

what_survives_unchanged: The TPS projection. ms_at_target = measured_ms * (target_bpw/current_bpw) uses only measured time and the BPW ratio, so 2.0 BPW -> 15.77 ms -> 63.4 TPS regardless of ceilings. If kernel headroom does exist, 63.4 TPS is a FLOOR rather than an estimate.
